prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
The Liberal Democrats pledge to build and safeguard a fair, free and open society, balancing liberty, equality and community, dispersing power, nurturing creativity, and ensuring no one is enslaved by poverty, ignorance or conformity. Their central choice for Britain is to stay open, generous and outward-looking—working with allies to face shared challenges.

Stop Brexit, build a brighter future
- Revoke Article 50 with a Lib Dem majority; otherwise, back a people’s vote with the option to remain.
- Protect jobs, the NHS, scientific collaboration and the Union; keep freedom of movement.
- Use a £50bn Remain Bonus to invest in schools, tackle inequality and boost public services.

A stronger, fairer, greener economy
- Invest £130bn in infrastructure: clean energy, transport, schools, hospitals and homes; create a Green Investment Bank.
- Rebalance the economy with devolved power and a £50bn Regional Rebalancing Programme.
- Make innovation-led growth the UK’s hallmark: raise R&D to 3% of GDP, expand Catapults, support creative industries and ethical tech.
- Back entrepreneurs and SMEs: prompt payment enforcement, start-up allowance, better access to capital, hyper-fast broadband.
- Fair taxes: restore corporation tax to 20%, replace business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy, clamp down on avoidance.
- Future of work: genuine Living Wage, new “dependent contractor” status with basic rights, day-one flexible work, stronger enforcement.
- Lifelong learning: £10,000 Skills Wallet for every adult; reform the apprenticeship levy into a wider Skills & Training Levy.
- Wellbeing first: introduce a wellbeing budget and impact assessments across government.

World-class education and skills
- Free, high-quality childcare from nine months for working parents (35 hours, 48 weeks); invest in Children’s Centres and early years.
- Reverse school cuts; hire 20,000 teachers; fix buildings; fund SEND properly.
- End “teaching to the test”: scrap mandatory SATs, replace Ofsted, protect arts, deliver a “curriculum for life.”
- Invest in FE and HE; restore maintenance grants; strengthen student mental health support.

Climate action now
- Net zero by 2045 at the latest; 80% renewable electricity by 2030; ban fracking.
- Insulate homes by 2030; end fuel poverty by 2025; zero-carbon standards for new buildings.
- Electrify rail, expand clean public transport, safe cycling and walking; all new cars electric by 2030.
- Restore nature: Nature Act, 60m trees/year, protect seas and green space; zero-waste, circular economy.

Health, care and mental health
- Raise £7bn/yr via a 1p income tax rise for the NHS and social care; £10bn capital upgrade.
- Parity for mental health: new waiting time standards, 24/7 crisis care, perinatal support, more talking therapies.
- Integrate health and social care; a dedicated workforce strategy; better support for carers.

A fair society that works for everyone
- Fix Universal Credit: five-day first payment, scrap two-child limit and benefit cap, right to food, fairer housing support.
- Housing: build 300,000 homes a year, including 100,000 for social rent; renters’ security; end rough sleeping in five years.
- Safer communities: restore community policing; a public health approach to violence; invest in youth services; focus on rehabilitation, not short sentences.

Freedom, rights and equality
- Defend the Human Rights Act and ECHR; protect civil liberties; end bulk surveillance and police facial recognition.
- Tackle hate crime; modernise gender recognition; end period poverty; improve accessibility.
- Compassionate immigration: end the hostile environment; 28-day detention limit; right to work after three months; expand refugee resettlement.

Better politics
- Fair votes (STV), votes at 16, votes for EU citizens settled long-term and all Brits abroad.
- Radical devolution and a written federal constitution for a united, home-rule UK.
- High-quality public debate: media standards, transparency in political ads, citizens’ assemblies.

A better world
- Pro-EU, multilateral leadership; 0.7% aid; climate diplomacy; Magnitsky sanctions; stricter arms controls (suspend sales to Saudi Arabia).
- Strong defence, NATO commitment, cyber resilience, minimum nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament.
- Recognise Palestine, uphold human rights, expand the BBC World Service, and lead global climate action.
